I've saved the 2025 Q3 results to `answer.json`. Run on Q2, the same logic reproduces all 10 reference values you gave.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `enterprise`, 262,533,981 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `svc`, 320,719,678 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-09` |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | `u148@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 233 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 640,655 |
| h. Growth from August to September | 19.2% |

**Interpretations the data required:** I tested each option against the Q2 values. Only one combination matched them all:
1. **Time zone:** Order times are stored in UTC (`...Z`). Many orders sit on either side of Korean midnight, at 14:30Z and 15:30Z. Converting to Korea time (UTC+9) before splitting by quarter and month is the only way to match Q2. Using UTC gives 18.4% growth for Q2 instead of 6.6%, and other values differ too.
2. **Duplicate customers:** 48 email addresses appear under two customer IDs each (300 IDs, 250 emails). Counting customers by email matches Q2 (233 customers, 203 repeat). Counting by ID gives 275 and 233. So customer counts and the refund ranking are by email.
3. **Segment names:** Values like `Enterprise `, `SMB` and ` consumer` differ in case and spacing. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping. The segment comes from the customer record attached to each order.

Calculations follow your definitions exactly: integer arithmetic with rounding down to whole won per line, and Decimal half-up rounding for the growth rate.
